title: Kasvu Therapeutics kehittää uutta tapaa hoitaa masennusta
content:
The drug development company Kasvu Therapeutics (Kasvu) put out announcing it has raised €30 million to develop pharmaceuticals for the treatment of major depressive disorder and other brain diseases. The amount is the largest ever raised for a Finnish pharmaceutical development company at the preclinical stage. 

The financing round was led by Norwegian venture capital investor Hadean Ventures focusing on drug development and health industry innovations. Finnish participants in the financing round included Tesi (Finnish Industry Investment Ltd), Innovestor Life Science Fund, Nordic Science Investments, Finnish Drug Discovery Center Ltd, Stephen Industries and University of Helsinki Funds.

The funding helps Kasvu’s lead drug candidate KTX-0141, meant for the treatment of depression, to proceed to initial clinical trials. It is expected to be trialled in humans as early as summer 2027. 

Kasvu’s story is based on long-term work by research groups of Neuroscience Center Research Director Eero Castrén and Professor of Biophysics Ilpo Vattulainen.

title: Kapsäkissa hatut viuhuvat ja roolit vaihtuvat
content:
Tuulikki Närhinsalo 

Kapsäkin uutuus vie 1400-luvun puoliväliin, Schlimmer-nimiseen saksalaiseen pikkukaupunkiin, mutta vain osaksi, sillä musikaalissa ollaan myös omassa ajassamme. Amerikkalaiskaverukset Doug ja Bud ideoivat ja kehittelevät käsikirjoitusta ja musiikkia Johannes Gutenbergistä kertovaan minimusikaaliin, jolle he toivovat menestystä Broadwaylla.

Anthony Kingin ja Scott Brownin käsikirjoittama ja säveltämä vauhdikas minimusikaali poukkoilee taitavasti Gutenberg-tarinan sekä Dougin – Joel Mäkinen ja Budin – Juha Pulli hyvin nykyaikaisen ajatusmaailman välillä. Siinä on niin aitoa hetkessä improvisoinnin ja keksinnän tuntua, että välillä melkein unohtuu, että jokainen repliikki on peräisin amerikkalaisesta käsikirjoituksesta.

title: Is this how the world ends? Extinction scenarios are taking over the AI debate.
content:
Aya Ibrahim, who leads national security work for the AI Now Institute, an independent research organization, said that any limitations of AI predictions may get little scrutiny from elected officials. Policymakers have a track record of being deferential when dealing with the tech sector, she said.

“When it comes to tech issues, there’s just this culture of learned helplessness from the same policymakers that sit on energy and commerce [committees] and oversee the FDA and prescription drugs,” topics where they don’t question their right to govern, said Ibrahim, a former Biden White House official. “Suddenly, if you can’t code the model yourself, then you’re not in a position to weigh in.”

title: Is Your City Using Axon License Plate Cameras? We Need Your Help
content:
Cities around the country are ditching Flock’s automatic license plate reader (ALPR) cameras, and replacing them with equivalent cameras from law enforcement contracting giant Axon. That move in large part comes in response to 404 Media’s coverage of how local cops performed lookups in Flock for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and how a cop in Texas searched Flock cameras nationwide to look for a woman who self-administered an abortion.

That brings up questions: what are cities and law enforcement agencies using Axon ALPRs for? And who are they in turn sharing that data with? 404 Media has started to find out, but needs the help of local residents and community members to figure out what is happening across the country.

title: "Extraordinary Rendition All Over Again": U.S. Deportees Sent to Equatorial Guinea Beaten, Imprisoned
content:
Two men deported from the United States to Equatorial Guinea were arrested by local police forces and transferred to a prison earlier this month, in apparent retaliation for speaking out about conditions they faced in the Central African country. Samson Birhane, who is from Eritrea, and Ahmed Soliman, a gay asylum seeker from Egypt, were both deported by the Trump administration despite U.S. immigration courts granting them protections.

On September 11, police forces arrived at Hotel Bamy in the city of Malabo, where more than two dozen people have been confined after their deportation from the United States to Equatorial Guinea, a country they have no ties to, as part of President Trump’s secretive “third-country” agreements. Birhane and Soliman say they were arrested and taken to prison for speaking out about the inhumane conditions endured by U.S. deportees at the hotel and threats by armed forces. While confined at the hotel, U.S. deportees have decried denial of medical care and legal assistance, and abuses they’ve described as psychological torture.

content:
Following the Call for Innovative Use Cases for the Cultural Heritage Cloud (HORIZON-CL2-2025-01-HERITAGE-03), ECHOES is delighted to welcome eight more Sister Projects.

CULTUR-ACT – Collaborative Use Case Living Labs Fostering Tools and ResoURces Validation and Adoption in the European Cloud for Next-Gen Digital Heritage Communities Cooperation

CULTURAL.ACT is designed as a real-world proving ground for the ECCCH, leveraging on a community of CHIs and CCIs – of diverse types, cultural heritage domains, disciplines, size and expertise – that agree to collaborate and share experiences in the use of ECCCH tools and resources in core tasks of their own processes and working environments.

HERITWIN – Cultural Heritage Digital Twins

HERITWIN strengthens Europe’s cultural resilience by validating the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH) through five real large-scale pilots in Sweden, Norway, Spain, The UK (Northern Ireland), and Greece. The project advances semantic digital twins, eXtended Reality reconstructions, preparedness modelling tools to support conservation, education, public engagement, tourism, and interoperable European data spaces.

title: EU Kids Act Won't Keep the Internet Accountable and Trustworthy
content:
The EU Commission draft law to restrict young people’s access to the internet that it presented last week will come at a high cost: it will put online services behind age gates, expand the use of intrusive age verification, and undermine the privacy of all users. 

The EU Kids Act aims to protect children from risks associated with social media, video games, and AI systems by introducing age-based access rules, safety requirements, and stronger enforcement and oversight measures. It presents itself as building on the Digital Services Act (DSA) and puts into “hard law” some of the safety-by-design measures specified in the non-binding DSA guidelines on minors’ protection. 

The proposal is built around the following elements: social media age “delay”, safety by design, age assurance and parental responsibility, and strong enforcement. Each of these measures are concerning.

title: What deep sea mining could mean for Jamaica’s fisherfolk
content:
‘Any activity that disrupts ocean health could have downstream consequences…’

Originally published on Global Voices

Image of an underwater shot of a vessel with a Jamaican flag on the bottom of its hull, created using Canva Pro elements.

For Jamaica’s fisherfolk, the sea has always been a critical source of food, livelihood, freedom and the future. It’s their pantry, workplace, and cultural centre, but as global companies look to the minerals lying deep below the ocean floor, questions emerge: what will happen to the fishers who rely on these waters when the seabed itself becomes a resource to be exploited?

The way that question is answered could shape the future of Jamaica’s fisheries, and resilience among communities is already bearing the brunt of climate change events. Deep-sea mining may generate sediment plumes, destroy habitats and reduce the biodiversity that cascades through the food chain, placing fisherfolk in the middle of an uncertain ocean economy.

title: Armenian Prisoners in Azerbaijan Allege Rights’ Violations
content:
Ruben Vardanyan, a former senior official in Nagorno-Karabakh's de facto administration who is serving a 20-year prison sentence in Azerbaijan, says that he and 18 other Armenian prisoners are being denied regular family contact, adequate exercise, medical tests, and other rights provided under Azerbaijani law.

In an audio appeal recorded on September 16 and published two days later, Vardanyan addressed Azerbaijan's human rights commissioner, Sabina Aliyeva. He said some prisoners at Umbaki prison do not receive weekly phone calls and none can make video calls. "When my cellmate was arrested, his child was 10 months old," Vardanyan said. "Now the child is more than 3 years old and has not seen his father."

Vardanyan said he has been unable to get medical tests even at his own expense, access notary services, or receive written responses to complaints. He said prisoners get only 20 to 40 minutes of outdoor exercise once a week, rather than an hour a day.

Human Rights Watch has not independently verified these allegations.

On September 19, Aliyeva’s office rejected the allegations that the prisoners’ rights were being violated.

Ulkoministeriön toimintamenoihin ehdotetaan 244 miljoonaa euroa. Toimintaympäristön kasvavissa paineissa ulkoasiainhallinto palvelee koko valtionhallintoa, kansalaisia, yrityksiä, järjestöjä, mediaa ja muita yhteistyökumppaneita.

title: Vetoomus kaikkein kehittyneimpien tekoälymallien hallinnan puolesta
content:
Syyskuu 2026

Tekoäly on voimakas teknologia. Sillä on potentiaalia parantaa ihmisten elämää, edistää tiedettä ja vahvistaa talouksiamme.

Samalla huipputason tekoälymallien nopea kehitys aiheuttaa vakavia turvallisuusriskejä, ellei kehitystä hallita asianmukaisesti.

Viime aikoina on havaittu, että kehittyneet tekoälyjärjestelmät ovat kiertäneet niiden testauksessa käytetyt suojatoimet, hyödyntäneet haavoittuvuuksia ja päässeet luvattomasti reaalimaailman järjestelmiin.

Johtavat tutkijat ja tekoäly-yhtiöiden johtajat varoittavat, että kehityksen vauhti saattaa ylittää kykymme hallita esiin nousevia riskejä.

Jotta tekoälyn hyödyt voidaan saavuttaa, yritysten, hallitusten ja yhteiskunnan on toimittava nyt. Meidän on puututtava näihin riskeihin ja vahvistettava valvontaa ilman, että kasvatamme samalla maiden välisiä eroja tekoälyn hyötyjen saatavuudessa.

Tekoälyn on pysyttävä ihmisten ohjauksessa, valvonnassa ja hallinnassa. Sitä on kehitettävä ja hyödynnettävä kansainvälisen oikeuden mukaisesti.

Kannatamme siksi viimeaikaisia aloitteita, joilla pyritään hallitsemaan kehittyneisiin teknologioihin liittyviä riskejä.

title: 22 countries back call to keep AI ‘under human control’
content:
NEW YORK — Several European countries were among a group of 22 nations that adopted a declaration Monday saying that artificial intelligence “must remain under human direction, oversight and control” and suggesting to create a global supervisory regime.

The declaration, adopted on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly this week, acknowledged AI’s “potential to improve lives, advance science and strengthen our economies” but warned that “the rapid development of frontier AI models poses serious risks to safety and security if not appropriately managed.”

The push comes ahead of the meeting of U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the leaders of the world’s leading AI-developing nations, in Washington Thursday.

Neither the U.S. nor China are part of the new declaration. But Finnish President Alexander Stubb, one of the main organizers of the document, told POLITICO that he hopes to create “momentum” and get more actors on board: “I think it will be in the interest of both China and the United States to have some kind of guardrails. And our message here is that we need human intervention, so humans need to be in charge,” he said in an interview.

title: ‘Small, flowering islands’: German city reveals how nature thrives when neighbours care for street tree beds
content:
When Olivia Besters began caring for the patch of soil beneath the chestnut tree outside her home in Freiburg, Germany, more than 35 years ago, biodiversity was not on her mind.

“It was the optics,” she told me. The ground was compacted and littered with trash and dog “legacies”. Besters simply wanted the space directly outside her front door to look nicer. “Everything else came much later,” she said. “Thirty-five years ago, no one talked about climate change or insect decline.”

Over time, one tree bed expanded into 36 across Besters’ neighbourhood of Herdern. So deep is her commitment to her tree beds that her children gifted her a bike trailer to cart around her watering system, her phone is filled with stunning pictures of the flowers growing in her tree beds, and she has been nominated for city-wide engagement awards.

As towns and cities grow, biodiversity is being squeezed into ever smaller spaces while people experience a progressive loss of everyday contact with nature. Street tree beds – and the practice of caring for them – offer cities a way to counter urban biodiversity loss while enriching people’s connection with nature in their neighbourhoods.

title: Forgotten Mozart notebook reveals how a young woman learned to compose
content:
A small notebook found in the Bibliothèque Nationale de France (the national library of France) has turned out to be one of the most important Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart discoveries in decades.

The 44 pages of the notebook document composition lessons that Mozart gave in Paris in 1778 to Marie-Louise-Philippine de Bonnières de Guînes, a highly accomplished young aristocratic harpist. The manuscript was recognised in February 2026 by François-Pierre Goy, a curator in the library’s music department who recognised Mozart’s handwriting in the unattributed notebook. Laurence Decobert, a specialist in Mozart’s manuscripts, agreed with him and Armin Brinzing, director of the Bibliotheca Mozartiana in Salzburg, later authenticated the document.

The notebook lets readers follow Mozart’s teaching from one exercise to the next. It also preserves something that composer-centred histories often miss: the musical work taking place around him, in this case by a young woman.

title: Kiusaaminen alkaa kauan ennen kuin se näyttää kiusaamiselta, sanoo tutkija
content:
Uudet tutkimustulokset osoittavat, että lasten ja nuorten keskinäiseen kiusaamiseen herätään liian myöhään. Kun asia tunnistetaan, ryhmässä on voinut olla pitkään käynnissä ilmiöitä, jotka ovat luoneet pohjan ulossulkemiselle, häirinnälle ja väkivallalle. Aikuisilla onkin keskeinen rooli varhaisessa tunnistamisessa.

"Kiusaaminen ei synny tyhjästä. Sitä edeltävät usein pienet, mutta merkitykselliset tilanteet, joissa lapset ja nuoret alkavat arvottaa, vertailla ja sulkea toisiaan ulkopuolelle. Juuri näihin hetkiin pitäisi kiinnittää nykyistä enemmän huomiota", Oulun yliopiston uuden oppituolin, nuorisotutkimuksen, professori Tuija Huuki kertoo tiedotteessa.

Tutkimus haastaa myös yleisen käsityksen siitä, että kiusaaminen johtuisi ensisijaisesti tietyistä "kiusaajista" tai "pahoista lapsista". Tulokset viittaavat siihen, että tavalliset lapset ja nuoret voivat tietyissä olosuhteissa alkaa vahingoittaa toisiaan.

Riski kasvaa erityisesti silloin, kun lasten ja nuorten väliset suhteet jäävät ilman aikuisen ohjausta.

title: "War on the Press": Trump Bans CNN, MS NOW & Politico from White House over Critical Coverage
content:
News organizations CNN, MS NOW and Politico are suing the Trump administration over the banning of their reporters from the White House on Friday. Their credentials were confiscated or deactivated when they attempted to enter White House grounds over the weekend. Trump’s decision is “sending the message that if you write stories that are critical of the president, you’re going to lose your access,” says Katie Fallow, a deputy litigation director at Columbia University’s Knight First Amendment Institute, where she focuses on threats to freedom of speech and of the press. “The real victims of this war on the press are members of the public, which are entitled to know about what their government is doing.”

Fallow says the White House press briefing room is a “public forum” and that “the courts have said repeatedly the government is not allowed to kick people out of that forum based on their viewpoint.”

title: The commodification of Indigenous cultures and traditions
content:
All too often, Indigenous traditions are extracted, repackaged, or seized for someone else’s gain

Originally published on Global Voices

A Huipil, Kaqchikel Maya, Patzun textile displayed in the Textile Museum of Canada, circa late 20th to early 21st c. Such textiles are an important Maya tradition and are still made by Maya weavers today. Image from Wikimedia Commons. CC0.

This post is part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” This series offers insight into the lives and experiences of Indigenous peoples to build connections across regions, center Indigenous experiences, and share the stories of leaders, activists, community members, and more. You can support this coverage by donating here.

For many Indigenous communities, the traditions, art, and ceremonies are the backbone of their shared identity, essential for marking important milestones, fostering a sense of community, and passing on histories to the younger generation. However, all too often, these traditions are extracted, repackaged, sold, or seized for someone else’s gain.

Broken Clay Pots: Part of a wedding ritual in Juchitán de Zaragoza, Oaxaca. Image from Flickr. CC BY-NC-ND 2.0

All too often, Indigenous traditions are extracted, repackaged, or seized for someone else’s gain

title: Another Journalist in Mali Sentenced to Prison
content:
A national cybercrime court in Mali on September 14 sentenced a prominent journalist, Abdramane Keïta, to two years in prison on bogus charges, in the military government’s latest attack on media freedom.

Security forces arrested Keïta, director of the newspaper Le Témoin (The Witness), on June 9 in Bamako, Mali’s capital, days after he commented on a television program that the Al-Qaeda-linked Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, or JNIM) controlled the northern city of Kidal. On April 25, JNIM and allied separatist fighters had launched coordinated attacks across Mali, killing the defense minister and seizing several northern cities, including Kidal. International media had widely reported that Kidal had fallen to the armed groups. 

On June 9, a prosecutor attached to the cybercrime court charged Keïta with “offense of a regional nature undermining national unity and the credibility of the state,” and put him in pretrial detention. His trial began on August 17.

title: EU pressures Big Tech to go green with new data center sustainability label
content:
BRUSSELS — Brussels on Monday unveiled an environmental rating scheme for data centers that power artificial intelligence, a move the EU’s energy chief described as the first step in pressuring tech giants into aligning with the continent’s climate efforts.

The new rules, which will apply from August 2027, oblige big data centers to display a label grading them on their energy efficiency, water usage and clean power uptake on a scale of A to G, much like the EU’s influential appliances ranking.

“This will add a lot of transparency and hopefully provide the incentives for these data centers to be as sustainable as possible,” said Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen in an interview with POLITICO ahead of the label’s presentation. 

The new label is optional for smaller data centers, “but later we are also going to introduce minimum performance standards which, of course, will put more pressure on those who may not voluntarily wish to be as sustainable as we want them to,” he added.

title: From French outpost to Euro-Canadian corridor? Why Carney and Macron met in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney did not need to cross the Atlantic to meet Emmanuel Macron on French soil over the weekend. Instead, he joined the French president in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, just 25 kilometres off Newfoundland.

It was the first official visit to the archipelago by a Canadian prime minister.

The visit brought together a contentious shared history, Canada’s rapprochement with Europe and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon’s search for new development opportunities.

Covering 242 square kilometres and home to around 6,000 people, the archipelago rarely attracts international attention. Yet its location gave the weekend meeting particular significance as France and Canada seek closer ties amid growing tensions with the United States.

After repeatedly threatening to make Canada a 51st state, U.S. President Donald Trump recently posted a map depicting an expanded U.S. encompassing Canada, Greenland and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.

Evidence of Indigenous presence in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon dates back nearly 5,000 years. It later attracted European explorers, including Frenchman Jacques Cartier in 1536.

title: As war in the Middle East widens, Saudi Arabia’s new defence pact could face a major test
content:
Last Thursday, US President Donald Trump said he had a “big decision” coming up about Iran’s regime:

Do I want to go in and annihilate them or do I not? […] Anything could happen with me.

Do I want to go in and annihilate them or do I not? […] Anything could happen with me.

This is not the first time he has spoken of such a threat. But it comes at a very critical juncture. A war he had once hoped to bring to a swift conclusion is now in its seventh month, and threatens to engulf more of the region.

Over the weekend, the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen said they had attacked “sensitive sites” in Saudi Arabia’s capital Riyadh with missiles and drones.

It’s an escalation that could put Saudi Arabia’s new defence agreement with Turkey and Pakistan – known as the “Mecca pact” – to its first serious test.

For Trump, failure to end this conflict in one way or another could also seriously jeopardise his remaining term in office and the United States’ standing in the world.

Several issues have brought the president to this point. Consumers in the US and across the world continue to suffer from intensified energy and economic impacts of the conflict.

title: US: Deportations to Haiti Endanger Lives
content:
(Washington, DC) – Since ending Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti in late July 2026, US authorities have deported hundreds of Haitians back to their country, where they face threats to their lives and safety and receive little to no support, Human Rights Watch said today. The US Senate should urgently pass House-approved legislation that would reinstate TPS for Haitians.

According to Haiti’s National Office for Migration (Office National de la Migration), more than 450 people have been deported from the United States to Haiti since July. Many had lived in the United States for years and were separated from US citizen family members, while others said they had pending asylum claims in the US. Haitian authorities lack the funding, staff, and policy frameworks to safely receive and assist deportees, Haitian government officials told Human Rights Watch.

“The United States is returning people, some with pending asylum claims, to a country that doesn’t have the capacity to protect them from violence, let alone help them find food and shelter,” said Nathalye Cotrino, senior Americas researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The US government should immediately halt these removals.”

title: Google hit with €403M privacy fine over handling of user location data
content:
The Irish data privacy authority fined Google €403 million on Monday over how it has been gathering location data from users.

This is the fourth largest fine ever issued by the Irish regulator and its first major penalty against Google. Ireland is charged with enforcing the European Union’s privacy rules against many of the world’s tech giants that have their European headquarters in Ireland.

The decision concludes an inquiry that was opened in 2020 by the Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC), following complaints from consumer organizations across the EU over how Google processed people’s location data and the transparency around that processing. 

Google infringed the General Data Protection Regulation, the EU’s landmark laws, on four counts, said Ireland’s three privacy commissioners Des Hogan, Dale Sunderland and Niamh Sweeney. The issues concerned how Google processed and retained location data in its Web & App Activity, Location History and Location Accuracy functions, as well as transparency.

The complaints from consumer groups alleged that Google had used dark patterns and unfair practices to incite users to enable features that shared their location data.

title: UN: Commit to Human Rights, Justice for Grave Crimes
content:
(New York) – World leaders at the annual meeting of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City from September 22-28, 2026, should commit to defending human rights, Human Rights Watch said. They should counter attempts to undermine accountability for grave international crimes and the work of the UN and other vital international institutions. 

Dozens of leaders and foreign ministers from the UN’s 193 member countries will attend the General Assembly’s general debate. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is scheduled to deliver the first speech on September 22, followed by US President Donald Trump. Others speaking on the first day include the leaders of Türkiye, France, the United Kingdom, and Japan.

“The UN and other international organizations created to protect human rights are under attack from countries that had pledged to defend them,” said Louis Charbonneau, UN director at Human Rights Watch. “All UN member countries should condemn attempts by the United States, Russia, China, and others to dismantle the international human rights system and destroy avenues for accountability for abuses.”

title: EU budget needs taxes governments aren’t already raising, Costa says
content:
DUBLIN — Governments will be more likely to back new EU taxes for the bloc’s next seven-year budget if they raise money that national governments are not already collecting, European Council President António Costa said.

In an interview with POLITICO, Costa set out for the first time what he gathered from leaders during his tour of 25 capitals on one of the thorniest issues in the talks: how to build support towards new EU levies — known as “own resources” — that would generate fresh revenue to the budget.

The answer will help determine whether EU governments can agree on a budget by the end of the year — before 2027’s elections in France, Italy, Spain and Poland threaten to derail the talks — without either cutting spending on new priorities or asking national governments to pay more.

“If we don’t create new own resources, we need to ask [for] more money from the member states,” Costa said. “We know that we need to keep the national contributions at a reasonable limit. For this, we need to have a credible basket of new own resources.”

Austragungsort ist die Konrad-Zuse-Stadt Hünfeld (Zuses Wahlheimat) – ein passender Ort für ein Wochenende zwischen Technik, Kreativität und neuen Ideen.

A 55-year-old physically challenged stranger appeared on the Bangladesh side of the India-Bangladesh border in Chapainawabganj in June 2026. By the time Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) reached him, a crowd had gathered around him.

He could not hold a pen — not because he did not know how to write, but because he had no fingers with which to hold it.

title: Global Poll: People Still Want the UN—But Want It to Deliver
content:
Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level debate, a 20-country survey finds strong support for international cooperation despite widespread anxiety about wars and the future.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 September 2026 (IDN) — The United Nations may be struggling with wars it cannot stop, divisions among the major powers and growing doubts about the international order. But a new global poll suggests that people are not ready to give up on either the UN or international cooperation.

They do, however, expect more.

A survey released by the United Nations Foundation on 17 September found that 57 per cent of respondents were worried about the future, while nearly nine in ten believed that even the world’s most powerful countries need the international system rather than trying to confront today’s problems on their own.

Only 13 per cent regarded the United Nations as outdated and no longer necessary.

But 52 per cent said the organisation remains necessary, even as it struggles to deliver results.

title: Digital Tribulations 25: Building Technological Sovereignty from Below, The Experience of Argentine Cooperativism – Interview with Cecilia Muñoz from Código Libre
content:
The introduction of Digital Tribulations, a series of intellectual interviews on the developments of digital sovereignty in Latin America, can be read here and the entire series can be found here.

During the month I spent in Buenos Aires, the last city I visited before finally flying back to Europe, I managed to get a firsthand look at its famous cooperativist scene, which extends to platforms. By “famous” I of course mean a niche that has accompanied platform studies since the sharing economy: platform cooperativism. I first came across it through the pioneering work of Trebor Scholz, and I became more familiar with it thanks to the prolific scholarship of my Brazilian friend Rafael Grohmann. He was the one who gave me Cecilia’s contact, along with the phone number of a fellow Italian, Stefano Tortorici, who is writing his PhD on platform cooperativism. As two Italian researchers in our semi-nomadic phase, I bonded with Stefano and ended up hanging out with his numerous artistic housemates, who shared a house not far from the gentrified Palermo neighborhood.

title: Disappearance of 2 Journalists in Djibouti Raises Concerns for Their Safety
content:
The Committee to Protect Journalists said Sunday that it is “deeply concerned” by reports that South African investigative journalist Micah Reddy and local fixer Kooki Mahmoud have gone missing in Djibouti, and urged authorities “to immediately clarify their whereabouts and ensure their safety.”

Contact with Reddy, the African coordinator for the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), and Mahmoud, a Djibouti-based journalist, was lost Saturday at approximately 1 p.m. local time, said an ICIJ statement. The statement, issued Sunday, said ICIJ is gravely concerned for their safety and authorities in Djibouti have not so far responded to its requests for information.

“We are calling on the government of Djibouti to: Immediately clarify Reddy and Mahmoud's whereabouts and confirm their well-being; Launch a prompt, transparent investigation into their disappearance; Keep their families, colleagues and employers fully and promptly informed,” the ICIJ statement said.

Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority recently released a Rapid Disaster Needs Assessment (RDNA) highlighting many of the challenges facing disaster-affected Nepalis, including the approximately 33,000 who have lost their homes.

As Nepal prepares long-term recovery and risk-reduction strategies, we offer insights from our collaborative research about post-disaster reconstruction and displacement following Nepal’s 2015 earthquake, as well as ongoing mountain hazards, to highlight areas of concern for the country’s affected communities.

title: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust
content:
US President Donald Trump is already presenting the new security agreement between the United States, Denmark and Greenland as a personal triumph.

By his telling, Washington has secured permanent control over Greenland’s security and the power to prevent adversaries from establishing military bases or making sensitive investments there.

The Prime Minister’s Office of Denmark describes a different bargain: stronger Arctic security that preserves the Kingdom of Denmark’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as Greenlanders’ right to self-determination.

Yet the political bargain is already visible. Trump gets the spectacle of power – or as a US correspondent for Danish newspaper Politiken said, “he was allowed to take a victory lap on social media”. Denmark and Greenland keep nominal sovereignty. NATO avoids an immediate rupture. Each party can declare success.

That is the optimistic reading. The more troubling one is that the agreement rewards months of coercion against an ally. It normalises a sphere-of-influence politics in which smaller states remain legally sovereign but face pressure to accept strategic subordination.

title: Pakistan: Rights Lawyers Rearrested after Bail
content:
(New York) – Pakistani authorities on September 17, 2026, rearrested human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha soon after the Supreme Court granted them bail, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should immediately release the two and drop the criminal charges against them, which appear aimed to punish peaceful expression and human rights advocacy.

The authorities had originally charged and convicted Mazari and Chattha, a married couple, for social media posts in support of local activists and criticizing the military. The Supreme Court on September 17 granted bail and ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final decision on their appeals. Hours later, the police rearrested Mazari and Chattha on anti-terrorism charges related to a separate, older case from March 2025 concerning their participation in a protest the authorities allege was illegal.

title: Africa’s Public-Sector Reforms Need Leaders, Not Only Technical Expertise
content:
The African Capacity Building Foundation and the Gates Foundation are expanding a programme designed to help officials turn sound policies into lasting institutional change.

By Jeffrey Moyo

HARARE, Zimbabwe | 19 September 2026 (IDN) — African governments must invest more seriously in leadership development if ambitious public-sector reforms are to produce lasting results, according to the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF) and the Gates Foundation.

The two organisations made the case during a 3 September webinar, “Leading Public Sector Transformation in Africa: Leadership Lessons from the LEAPS Programme”. The discussion examined how stronger leadership could help governments overcome resistance to reform, improve public financial management and turn policy initiatives into measurable institutional gains.

Mamadou Biteye, ACBF’s Executive Secretary, said public-sector reform in Africa was rarely held back by a shortage of good ideas.

“More often, the real challenge is our ability to lead change by bringing people together, building trust, overcoming resistance, and sustaining momentum,” he said.

title: “Our Dear Friend Umar”: How We Uncovered That a Russian Oligarch Bankrolled Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding
content:
My colleagues and I had been digging for days. We’d heard a rumor that a Russian oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin named Umar Kremlev had attended Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding this past May in the Bahamas. But to confirm that, we needed visual proof. 

First, we scoured everything the Trumps had released from the event, held on a pair of private islands. On social media and in the pages of tabloids such as Page Six and Hello! magazine, official photos from the weekend showed an intimate chapel ceremony alongside lavish beach parties. Several photos depicted guests, including Jared Kushner and Eric Trump, and we scanned them all for signs of Kremlev. Still, nothing had turned up yet.

We then turned to Kremlev’s social media profiles on the off chance that he’d posted about the wedding. Incredibly, on Telegram, Kremlev had posted videos over the same weekend as Trump Jr.’s wedding that appeared to be from someplace tropical. In one, a single detail caught our attention: As Kremlev speaks in Russian to the camera, the frame gives a partial view of an outdoor patio setting. It wasn’t palm trees or crystal water we noticed, but the wicker furniture.

title: What’s really motivating these AI apocalypse stories?
content:
AI Now’s co-executive director Sarah Myers West joins Al Jazeera’s The Listening Post to talk about regulating the tech industry, and the familiar race to the bottom we see playing out in front of us.

“Time and again, whenever we’ve seen any movement toward meaningful regulation of the tech industry, we see a revival of this [race] narrative,” says Myers West. “What this narrative mistakes though is that regulation of the sector actually would be a tremendous boon to competition. Nobody is helped if we have an unregulated sector that’s engaged in the race to the bottom. That’s what we’re seeing right here and now.”

title: Statement: AlgorithmWatch im Innenausschuss zu KI-basierter Überwachung: Biometrische Massenerkennungssysteme müssen verboten werden!
content:
Berlin, 18. September 2026 – Am Montag, den 21. September 2026, behandelt der Innenausschuss des Deutschen Bundestags die Gesetzentwürfe zur Massenüberwachung mittels Biometrie und KI-Systemen für das Bundeskriminalamt, die Bundespolizei und das Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge, die das Bundesministerium des Innern (BMI) und das Bundesministerium der Justiz und für Verbraucherschutz (BMJV) vorgelegt haben. Pia Sombetzki, Senior Policy Managerin bei AlgorithmWatch, wurde von der Linksfraktion als Sachverständige eingeladen und wird in ihrer Stellungnahme erneut die Gesetzeswidrigkeit der vorgeschlagenen Maßnahmen betonen und die vollständige Rücknahme der Entwürfe sowie ein grundsätzliches gesetzliches Verbot des Einsatzes biometrischer Massenerkennungssysteme für öffentliche und private Stellen fordern.

Damit unterstreicht AlgorithmWatch die bereits vielfach geäußerte Kritik an den Gesetzen: Die vorgeschlagenen Befugnisse sind europarechtswidrig, verletzen verfassungsrechtliche Mindestanforderungen und widersprechen datenschutzrechtlichen Grundsätzen.

Pia Sombetzki hebt hervor: „Die Bundesregierung schafft mit den Gesetzen nichts anderes als die technische Voraussetzung für eine flächendeckende Verfolgung aller Menschen im öffentlichen Raum. Im Internet öffentlich zugängliche Daten können so gut wie alles umfassen, sowohl das Foto von der letzten Demonstration als auch das Urlaubsvideo mit den Kindern. All diese Daten zu erfassen, ist weder erforderlich für die Arbeit von Ermittlungs- und Strafverfolgungsbehörden noch verhältnismäßig. Allerdings hat es eine zutiefst einschüchternde Wirkung: Menschen wissen zukünftig nicht, ob, wann und wie Foto-, Video- oder Tonaufnahmen von ihnen durch KI-Systeme von Polizei- oder Migrationsbehörden ausgewertet werden.

title: "We Are the 99%": 15 Years Later, Occupy Wall Street's Impact Is Still Being Felt
content:
Fifteen years ago this week, thousands of activists marched on the Financial District in New York City. They formed the Occupy Wall Street encampment in Zuccotti Park, launching a movement focused on economic inequality that spread across the nation and globe under the slogan, “We are the 99%.” Protesters would go on to sleep in Zuccotti Park for nearly two months before police raided the encampment.

“Occupy Wall Street changed the public’s common sense about class and class struggle and inequality in this country,” says Yotam Marom, who helped organize the Occupy protests in New York City. “It’s hard to see how you get a Bernie Sanders 2016 run without the public shifting its relationship to that story.”

Marom says Occupy participants were inspired by mass protests happening around the world at that time, including the Arab Spring and the anti-austerity movement in Spain known as the Indignados.

Still, “We got it wrong on a lot of things. We had a ton of internal conflict that really jeopardized the project,” he says.

Marom’s new book is For Louder Days: Reaching Beyond a Politics of Powerlessness.

title: What does a stronger Europe actually require? Demos Helsinki’s comments on the State of the Union.
content:
President von der Leyen highlighted in her State of the Union speech on 16 September a Europe that must become more capable of acting on its own terms: stronger in defence, more secure in energy, more competitive in technology, and more resilient in the face of climate and social pressures.

However, strengthening Europe is not only a question of ambition. It raises difficult questions about dependencies, governance and what we actually mean by resilience. Drawing on research from three EU-funded projects, we look at some of the tensions behind the speech: what technological sovereignty requires in practice, how climate resilience depends on institutions that can work across policy silos, and why Europe’s strength cannot be measured solely through current economic indicators.

title: How Poland “planned to occupy Czech lands” – coordinated information operation exposed
content:
Facebook posts called on people to gather for a protest in the Czech border town of Třinec on Saturday, 29th of August. The protest never took place. The Třinec municipal authorities had already announced that no public event had been registered, while the Czech Republic’s largest trade union, KOVO, which represents metalworking and industrial workers and whose logo was used in the protest advertising materials, denied any connection with the action. Moreover, Polish and Czech media had already exposed the disinformation campaign, which involved fake social media profiles, fabricated media outlets, forged documents and even an unauthorised publication of an article on the website of a public broadcaster.

At the beginning of August, disinformation began circulating claiming that Poland planned to take over more than 600 hectares of Czech territory. According to an analysis by the Czech news portal Seznam Zprávy, several social media accounts in the Czech Republic circulated a document purportedly sent by the Polish government to the Czech authorities. It allegedly demanded that land with a total area of 638.44 hectares be handed over to Poland.

title: EFF Statement on California Governor's Executive Order on AI
content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom's executive order is an opportunity for a needed, thoughtful conversation about artificial intelligence and its potential harms. Everyday Californians are feeling real anxiety about the risks of artificial intelligence, and as an organization that works to ensure technology empowers people, EFF welcomes this order as a way for the state of California to lead a much-needed dialogue that addresses these concerns. 

Nonetheless, the most immediate and current concerns with this technology are not about sci-fi scenarios concerning rogue super-intelligence. They are happening right now through biased algorithmic decision-making for employment or government benefits, AI-powered surveillance systems such as Flock cameras, and artificially inflated personalized pricing. People want state and federal leaders to act, and we urge Gov. Newsom to develop thoughtful policies to address those concerns. Today’s EO is a good start.

Elinkeinoelämän tutkimuslaitos on nostanut kuluvan vuoden kasvuennustettaan. Bkt:n ennustetaan kasvavan tänä vuonna 1,7 prosenttia. Suomi myös pysyttelee kasvussa kiinni lähivuosina ja ensi vuonna kasvuksi ennustetaan jo liki kaksi prosentia. Erityisesti investoinnit tuottavat kasvusysäyksen. Ensi vuoden investointien kasvu tulee suurelta osin hakukoneyhtiö Googlen ilmoittamista datakeskusinvestoinneista. Suhdannewebinaarissa keskusteltiin hyvien kasvu-uutisten lisäksi myös velkajarrusta sekä työmarkkinoiden tilasta.

Elinkeinoelämän tutkimuslaitos julkisti vuoden toisen laajan talousennusteensa, syksyn Suhdanteen, torstaina 17.9. Etlan ennusteen mukaan Suomen kasvukäänne vahvistuu ja investointihanat aukeavat. Suomi myös pysyttelee kasvussa kiinni tulevina vuosina.

Suhdanteen julkistuswebinaarissa ensimmäisen Suhdanne-ennusteensa esitteli Etlan pääekonomisti Jenni Pääkkönen. Toimitusjohtaja Aki Kangasharju piti alkuun lyhyen talouspoliittisen katsauksen. Webinaarin juonsi Etlan viestintäjohtaja Tytti Sulander.

title: Maailman ympäri sähkörekalla - Tobias Wagner aloittaa kiertomatkan Hampurista sunnuntaina 20.9
content:
Saksalainen Tobias Wagner, joka tunnetaan myös nimellä ”Elektrotrucker”, aloittaa sunnuntaina IAA Transportation -messuilta maailmanympärimatkansa Mercedes-Benz eActros 600 -kuorma-autolla. Kokenut kuorma-autonkuljettaja ja sisällöntuottaja pyrkii olemaan ensimmäinen henkilö, joka kiertää maailman sähköisellä pitkän matkan kuorma-autolla noin vuoden kuluessa julkiseen latausinfraan tukeutuen.

Yli 30 maata ja 80 latausta

Wagnerin reitti on pituudeltaan noin 45 000 kilometriä ja kulkee noin 30 maan kautta Euroopassa, Aasiassa, Australiassa, Pohjois-Amerikassa ja Etelä-Amerikassa. Matka on tarkoitus toteuttaa enintään 80 latauspysähdyksellä. Löytöretken tavoitteena on dokumentoida sähköisen kuorma-auton teknistä suorituskykyä erilaisissa maantieteellisissä, ilmastollisissa ja infrastruktuuriin liittyvissä olosuhteissa sekä samalla edistää keskustelua tieliikenteen tavaraliikenteen latausinfrastruktuurin laajentamisesta.

title: British-Turkish novelist and storyteller Elif Shafak wins Helena Vaz da Silva European Award 2026
content:
Press release English – Portuguese

The acclaimed British-Turkish author Elif Shafak is the winner of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness on Cultural Heritage 2026. This European recognition pays tribute to Elif Shafak’s exceptional ability to bring Europe’s rich and diverse cultural heritage to life through her captivating storytelling, while responding to the challenges of our time with a powerful call for defending democracy, promoting solidarity, embracing cosmopolitanism and celebrating cultural diversity.

Elif Shafak – Photo credit: Ferhat Elik

The Helena Vaz da Silva European Award was established in 2013 by the Centro Nacional de Cultura (Portugal) in collaboration with Europa Nostra and the Portuguese Press Club, and has the support of the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Portugal, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation and Tourism of Portugal.

The award ceremony will take place on 5 November at the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, Portugal.

title: Moscow cries fraud abroad while fixing the vote at home
content:
Moscow routinely portrays elections in democratic countries as fraudulent and controlled from abroad. Yet Russia’s own parliamentary election offers no genuine political choice: the Kremlin controls the field and has eliminated even the possibility of voting against the war in Ukraine. As the war’s effects reach deeper into everyday life, growing public dissatisfaction is being kept out of the ballot box.

When post-Soviet states turn away from Russia, as Armenia or Moldova have done, Kremlin officials and aligned outlets usually blame Western interference. Yet Moscow has itself tries to influence elections through foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI), often alongside financial support for pro-Russian groups. Moldovan authorities say Russian agents spent about €200 million – nearly 1% of Moldova’s GDP – on vote-buying and disinformation during the country’s 2024 presidential election and EU referendum. Investigators later found that the sanctioned Russian organisation Evrazia had used similar tactics ahead of Armenia’s 2026 election. Moscow nevertheless portrayed EU assistance intended to counter such threats as election interference.

title: Samtal om Själö hospital – kvinnoöden på 1800-talet
content:
Tidpunkt: 26.10 klockan 18.00-19.00
Plats: Finlandsinstitutet
Adress: Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Språk: svenska
Inträde: Gratis, men anmäl dig gärna här gärna här

Berättelsen om Själös kvinnoöden fortsätter att fascinera den finländska befolkningen och är igen aktuell i och med den nya finländska långfilmen Berätta för alla. På Själö, en ö i Åbolands skärgård, har ett av Finlands äldsta sjukhus fungerat i över 350 år. Men det var på 1800-talet som sjukhuset mer eller mindre förvandlades till ett sjukhus för enbart kvinnor. Kvinnor som beskrevs som obotligt sjuka men som i hög grad bestod av individer som samhället helt enkelt inte ville veta av. Och de allra flesta kvinnor som kom till Själö blev kvar resten av livet.

I samband med premiären av Berätta för alla ordnar vi ett samtal om Själös kvinnoöden och kanske ställer vi oss frågan, hade också jag hamnat där? För hur ser den samhälleliga blicken på kvinnor egentligen ut idag och vad är det med Själö som fortsätter att beröra?

I samtalet deltar bland annat författaren Johanna Holmström som skrivit boken Själarnas ö och skådespelaren Marketta Tikkanen från den högaktuella filmen Berätta för alla.

title: Sweden’s 2026 election: Social Democrats lost the battle but won the war?
content:
In last week’s parliamentary elections in Sweden, the Swedish Social Democratic Party undoubtedly became the largest party, with the support of 28 per cent of voters and a strong chance of leading the next government by replacing the incumbent right-wing one. Yet, within Swedish Social Democracy, a sense of dissatisfaction prevails. How did this come about?

In a fragmented parliament with eight parties, 28 per cent of the popular vote is not a disaster – especially not from a European perspective. When conservative Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson steps down after four years, it will be the first time since 1994 that a Swedish government has lost power after only a single term.

Yet the 2-point drop to 28 per cent remains historically weak for the Social Democrats. Above all, the contrast with the preceding term is striking. For periods, the party polled between 35 and 37 per cent, and as recently as August, the centre-left opposition bloc held a lead of around ten percentage points. When the results came in, however, the election was decided by a razor-thin margin.

title: Venezuela: Reform Needed for Rights Progress
content:
(Washington, DC) – Venezuela needs to take urgent measures and carry out institutional reforms to protect people’s basic rights, Human Rights Watch said today, following its first official visit to the country since 2008. 

Human Rights Watch visited Caracas this week and met with interim President Delcy Rodríguez, other government officials, human rights groups, members of the opposition, journalists, relatives of political prisoners, foreign diplomats, and others. Staff also visited Petare, a low-income neighborhood on the outskirts of Caracas. During its previous high-level visit, in 2008, Venezuelan authorities detained Human Rights Watch staff after they released a report and expelled them from the country.

“Interim President Delcy Rodríguez has overseen a pause to the most overt forms of repression in Venezuela,” said Federico Borello, deputy executive director at Human Rights Watch. “But in this fragile political moment, these gains will only become sustainable with robust institutional reforms and the release of all political prisoners.”

title: What Shall We Do About South Africa?
content:
By Azu Ishiekwene

The writer is the Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and the author of the new book Writing for Media and Monetising It.

ABUJA, Nigeria | 18 September 2026 (IDN) — If South Africa needed any serious signal that the mobs roaming the streets of its cities and townships in search of immigrants were a disgrace, the FIFA World Cup in June 2026 provided a large screen.

But the country is not looking. Or is looking but cannot see.

In the last three years, according to Xenowatch, about 50 people have been killed in xenophobic-related incidents in South Africa. That’s not counting the displaced and wounded or the hundreds forcibly repatriated, and those whose businesses have been destroyed.

Between June 2026 and now, there have been eight verified deaths linked to xenophobic attacks on Africans. Two of them, Bishop Taiwo Michael Fakunle and James Uchechukwu Nwankwo, were Nigerians. The Ghanaian News Agency reported that two Ghanaians were killed between July and August.

What will it take to end this madness, which has set one of Africa’s most promising countries against the rest of the continent?

title: Eskarilaisten vanhemmat kutsutaan kirjastoon
content:
Miten lasten lukuinto syntyy? Samalla tavalla kuin miten he muutenkin elämää oppivat. Aikuisten esimerkin kautta.

Tämän ovat oivaltaneet Oriveden kirjastoammattilaiset, kirjastonhoitajat Mia Moilanen ja Ilkka Kaita-aho sekä varhaiskasvatuksen opettaja Tanja Riihimäki, jotka aloittivat pari vuotta sitten kirjaston vanhempainillat esikoululaisten perheille.

Syksyn alkaessa esikoulun aloittaneet ja heidän vanhempansa kutsutaan kirjastoon seikkailemaan ja saamaan tietoa siitä, mitä kaikkea kirjasto perheille tarjoaa.

Myös perheiden muut lapset ovat tervetulleita iltaan, sillä tarkoitus on herättää koko perheen yhteinen kiinnostus kirjojen maailmaan. Näin kirjaston avulla täydennetään neuvolasta alkanutta lukemisen pariin kannustamista.

Vanhempainillan aikana kirjasto on varattu pelkästään eskareiden perheille. Ensimmäisellä kerralla mukana oli sata osallistujaa, eli lähes kaikki pienen paikkakunnan esikoululaiset perheenjäsenineen.

title: 6 Yleiset käsittelyperusteet
content:
Henkilötietojen käsittely tietosuoja-asetuksen 6 artiklan 1 kohdan c alakohdan nojalla on lainmukaista, jos se on tarpeen rekisterinpitäjän lakisääteisen velvoitteen noudattamiseksi. Lakisääteinen velvoite on henkilötietojen käsittelyperusteena suppeampi käsite kuin kunnan lakisääteinen tehtävä: lakisääteinen velvoite edellyttää, että toimijalle on tehtäväänsä liittyen säädetty nimenomaisia velvoitteita. 

Lakisääteisen velvoitteen tulee perustua Euroopan unionin tai kansalliseen lainsäädäntöön. Kyseeseen voivat tulla myös lakia alemman asteiset säännökset ja määräykset. Jotta lakisääteinen velvoite soveltuu käsittelyperusteeksi, WP29-tietosuojatyöryhmän tulkintaohjeiden 6/2014 (Lausunto direktiivin 95/46/EY 7 artiklan mukaisesta rekisterinpitäjän oikeutetun intressin käsitteestä WP217) mukaan myös kaikkien seuraavien edellytysten on täytyttävä:

  • Velvoite on riittävän selvä sen edellyttämän henkilötietojen käsittelyn suhteen.
  • Velvoite on sitova. Rekisterinpitäjällä ei saa olla valinnanvaraa sen suhteen, noudattaako se velvoitetta vai ei, eikä kohtuutonta harkinnanvaraa siinä, miten se noudattaa velvoitetta.

title: OKM: selvitys esittää tekijänoikeusjärjestöille lakisääteistä asiavaltuutta
content:
Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriön julkaisema selvitys ehdottaa, että tekijänoikeusjärjestöjen asiavaltuudesta säädetään lailla. Muutos helpottaa teosten luvattomaan käyttöön puuttumista erityisesti silloin, kun käyttö koskee suurta määrää teoksia.

Taiteilijan voi olla vaikea valvoa, miten hänen teoksiaan käytetään. Tekijänoikeusjärjestöillä on oikeuksien hallinnointiin valtuutuksia, mutta ne eivät voi lähtökohtaisesti viedä omissa nimissään tekijänoikeuden loukkauksia oikeuteen, jollei yksinoikeuksia ole siirretty järjestöille. Asia nousi esiin korkeimman oikeuden (KKO 2024:53) ratkaisussa, jossa KKO katsoi, ettei Kopiostolla ollut asiavaltuutta eli oikeutta esittää omissa nimissään vaatimuksia tekijänoikeuden loukkausta koskevassa jutussa.

OKM:n tilauksesta asiantuntijaselvityksen tehnyt emeritusprofessori Niklas Bruun esittää, että asiavaltuudesta säädetään lailla. Bruunin mukaan tekijänoikeusjärjestöillä on välitön intressi valvoa oikeuksia, sillä ne hallinnoivat tekijänoikeuksia ja lähioikeuksia kollektiivisesti, oikeudenhaltijoiden yhteiseen lukuun.

title: Purkutaiteen 10-vuotisnäyttely käsittelee epämukavia aiheita mutta tarjoaa myös rauhoittumisen paikkoja
content:
Ai tätä trendisanalla ”immersiivinen taide” tarkoitetaan! Sen hoksaa, kun vaeltaa Arabian 135-korttelin käytävillä, entisissä studioissa ja luokkahuoneissa.

Keväällä avatussa Purkutaide-kollektiivin 10-vuotisnäyttelyssä Tämän haluan sanoa on esillä 55 tilataideteosta, joiden luomaan maailmaan voisi helposta upota koko päiväksi.

Kollektiivi uskoo moniaistillisuuteen ja kokemuksellisuuteen ja pyrkii siihen, että kaikki tuntevat olonsa tervetulleiksi. Sekä taideharrastajat että vähemmän kokeneet kävijät voivatkin löytää teosten kuva-, väri-, ääni- ja tekstimaailmasta uusia tapoja hahmottaa todellisuutta ja erilaisia yhteiskunnallisia ilmiöitä.

Asia on painavaa. Omiin huoneisiinsa erotellut teokset käsittelevät muun muassa pikamuotia, ekologista kriisiä, tuotantoeläinten asemaa, sukupuolta, mielenterveysongelmia ja muistisairautta.

title: Bosnia Seizes 1.1 Tons of Synthetic Drugs Worth Up to €33 Million
content:
Authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina have seized nearly 1.1 metric tonnes of dangerous synthetic cathinones with a potential street value of up to 33 million euros ($37.82 million), and arrested two suspects, marking the largest synthetic drug bust in the history of the nation of roughly 3.5 million people, the State Border Service announced.

The seized substance—an extremely dangerous stimulant used as a substitute for cocaine and ecstasy—carries a wholesale market value of 5 million euros ($5.73 million), but its street value skyrockets when broken down into individual grams sold at 20 to 30 euros ($23 to $34.50) each across the region, according to the Border Police. In addition to the massive drug cache, officers confiscated a firearm, mobile phones, corporate documentation, official stamps, and specialized full-face respirator masks with advanced air-filtration systems used to protect operators during chemical synthesis and drug "cooking." The Border Police noted that investigators have not yet established the origin or final destination of the shipment, as the investigation remains ongoing.

title: Rage Against the Machines: From the Luddites to the AI Data Center Backlash
content: One often-repeated anecdote about Milton Friedman has the famous economist visiting a canal under construction in nineteen-sixties China. Noticing the sheer number of human laborers digging away with shovels, he asked the official in charge why they weren’t getting the work done faster with excavators and other modern machines. The bureaucrat explained to him that doing it by hand created more jobs. Friedman’s reply: “If it’s jobs you want, you should give those men spoons instead.” Whether or not this exchange ever actually happened, it illustrates a conflict that’s arisen more than once in the history of civilization, possibly since the dawn of industrialization — and at least since the heyday of the Luddites.

Yleisöllä oli mahdollisuus tutustua tasavallan presidentin virka-asuntoon Mäntyniemeen perjantaina 18. syyskuuta 2026. Avoimien ovien päivänä Mäntyniemessä kävi 2 100 vierasta.

Neljä tuntia kestäneen tapahtuman aikana pääsi tutustumaan tasavallan presidentin edustustiloihin. Reitti kulki pääaulasta Mäntyniemen pieneen ja suureen salonkiin sekä edelleen ruokasaliin. Myös presidentin työhuoneeseen oli mahdollista kurkistaa. Kierroksen lopuksi vierailtiin Mäntyniemen puutarhassa.

Reitin varrella oli presidentin kanslian henkilökuntaa vastaamassa kysymyksiin. Myös Mäntyniemeen sijoitetun taiteen tekijöitä oli kertomassa teoksistaan. Paikalla olivat taiteilijat Mayumi Niiranen-Hisatomi, Kimi Pakarinen, Osmo Rauhala ja Kimmo Schroderus.

Kiitos kaikille Mäntyniemessä vierailleille!

title: Judge Denies Efforts to End Oversight of Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office as Racial Profiling of Latinos Persists
content:
A federal judge has denied efforts to remove oversight of the Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office, saying the agency continues to show racial disparities in traffic arrests of Latinos — and that there is not enough evidence that efforts to improve would stick without legal monitoring.

In his 72-page ruling issued Sept. 10, U.S. District Judge G. Murray Snow stressed Sheriff Jerry Sheridan’s role in the department’s racial profiling since the start of the case more than a decade ago, including fighting court-ordered reforms and stymieing investigations. Sheridan was the No. 2 under former Sheriff Joe Arpaio when the county was found out of compliance with federal law.

“Then Chief Deputy, now Sheriff, Sheridan in particular was found to have abused his authority over MCSO’s internal affairs process by obstructing and manipulating misconduct investigations and disciplinary proceedings — including those involving himself — to shield deputies and Command Staff from accountability and undermine the enforcement of remedies designed to address the constitutional violations against the Plaintiff class,” the judge wrote in an opinion that mentions Sheridan 30 times.

title: Keskustelu Seilin sairaalasta – naisten kohtalo 1800-luvulla
content:
Aika: 26.10 kello 18.00-19.00
Paikka: Finlandsinstitutet
Osoite: Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Kieli: Ruotsi
Sisäänpääsy: Imainen mutta ilmoittaudu mielellään täällä

Tarina Seilin saaren naisten kohtalosta kiehtoo yhä suomalaisia, ja on nyt noussut jälleen pinnalle uuden elokuvan Kerro kaikille myötä. Turun saaristossa sijaitsevalla Seilin saarella sijaitsee yksi Suomen vanhimmista sairaaloista, joka on toiminut jo yli 350 vuotta. Mutta vasta 1800-luvulla sairaala muuttui käytännössä vain naisille tarkoitetuksi laitokseksi. Naiset, joita kuvailtiin parantumattomiksi yksilöiksi, olivat suurin osa vain ihmisiä joista yhteiskunta ei halunnut tietää. Monet näistä naisista jäivät Seilin saarelle loppuelämäkseen.

Kerro kaikille elokuvan yhteydessä järjestämme keskustelun Seilin naisten kohtalosta, kysyen ehkä myös itseltämme, olisinko minäkin jäänyt saarelle? Millainen on yhteiskunnan suhtautuminen naisiin nykyään, ja mikä Seilin saaressa vielä tänäkin päivänä koskettaa?

Keskusteluun osallistuvat muun muassa kirjailija Johanna Holmström, joka on kirjoittanut kirjan Sielujen saari, sekä näyttelijä Marketta Tikkanen, joka näyttelee elokuvassa Kerro kaikille.

title: California’s Newsom signs executive order to explore new AI rules, consider ‘kill switch’
content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order on Friday to speed up two AI laws he recently signed and explore proposals like requiring that AI companies develop a “kill switch” for their most advanced models.

The order comes after the Democrat told POLITICO this week he was mulling his options to take further action on AI safety, including a possible special legislative session to address recent safety concerns set off by AI researchers’ warnings that the technology could pose an existential risk to humanity and prominent autonomous hacking incidents.

Newsom said his executive action was also driven by federal inaction, after President Donald Trump responded to the warnings by dismissing them as a “hoax” and saying the only guardrails AI needs are his presidency. On Friday, Newsom urged Trump and Congress to adopt California’s AI framework or use the state’s existing regulations as a floor for federal rules.

“The federal government’s abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation,” Newsom said in his press release.

title: Why Europe has been absent from the great AI safety debate
content:
Though Europe has measures that address how consumers might encounter AI, technology will impact them if the worst scenarios bear

Europe’s dilemma over AI was rendered in stark terms this week. The head of the continent’s central bank, Christine Lagarde, said Europeans have two options: shun the technology and lose out on growth; or embrace it and become dependent on tools developed by the US and China.

The great debate over AI safety that has erupted in recent days threatens to make the choice moot. If the worst scenarios come to bear – and experts have differing views on this – then the technology will impact the continent regardless.

title: What might Canada’s EU ‘associate membership’ look like, and is it even a possibility?
content:
In a speech to the European Parliament, Canadian prime minister Mark Carney declared that “Europe and Canada are stronger together”. He also backed an offer made by the president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, one day earlier for Canada to become the first “associate member” of the bloc.

“Canada welcomes this ambition,” he said. “An alliance for the future is a unique, positive approach that we will define together.” But what might associate membership look like, how significant is von der Leyen’s offer in the history of the EU’s relations with external states, and how likely is it to come into being?

Canada already has a preferential trade deal with the EU in the form of the 2016 Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (Ceta). This type of free-trade agreement is typical of the sort of legal instrument used by the EU to manage relations with its main international partners.

But one way in which the EU could upgrade Ottawa’s relations with Brussels would be to look to the template of the “association agreements” the EU uses to bring neighbouring countries into closer alignment with its policies and programmes.

title: When does being ‘apolitical’ become a political act? An ethicist on the Ed Sheeran saga
content:
Headlines this week have been inundated with news of artist Macklemore being dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour, following Macklemore’s onstage calls to “free Palestine”.

The rap artist said Robert Kraft, owner of New England Patriots and the Gillette Stadium, barred him from playing in his stadium, and rallied other stadiums to join the boycott.

In response, Sheeran’s remaining support acts also withdrew. Sheeran has attempted to distance himself from the decision, suggesting it was the promoter’s and not his. He has taken an “apolitical” stance, referring back to his history of avoiding public political statements.

But the resulting condemnation from fans and commentators suggests forcing neutrality in such situations isn’t straightforward.

Politics isn’t limited to government. In a more general sense, it refers to the relationships of power in society and between members of society, and efforts to change them.

title: Johtajan nimissä tuleva kiireellinen maksupyyntö voi olla huijaus
content:
Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskukselle ilmoitetaan säännöllisesti huijauksista, joissa rikollinen esiintyy organisaation johtajana ja yrittää saada työntekijän siirtämään rahaa.

Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskukselle on raportoitu tapauksia, joissa huijari esittää olevansa esimerkiksi pääjohtaja, kunnanjohtaja, arkkipiispa, rehtori, pormestari tai pääsihteeri.

Huijarit selvittävät etukäteen organisaation johtoa ja työntekijöiden tehtäviä. Johtajan nimiin väärennetyllä viestillä rikollinen yrittää saada työntekijää tekemään maksun tai hankinnan. Valejohtaja voi pyytää työntekijää hankkimaan lahjakortteja liikelahjoiksi tai maksamaan laskun ilman tavanomaisia tarkastuskäytäntöjä. Usein verukkeena on, että johtaja on kokouksessa eikä voi vastata puheluihin, mutta asia pitää hoitaa kiireesti ja kyselemättä.

title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu vuodenvaihteen jälkeen – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Vihreiden Harjanteelta ja Elolta ehdotus: Hakkuita voisi ohjata luonnon ennallistamiseen
content:
Vihreiden kansanedustajat Atte Harjanne ja Tiina Elo ehdottavat, että hakkuita suunnataan nykyistä enemmän soiden ennallistamiskohteisiin Suomessa. Kansanedustajien mukaan malli voisi yhdistää puunkorjuun ja luontokadon torjunnan.

Harjanne ja Elo muistuttavat, että suoluonnon ennallistamisessa keskeistä on paitsi ojien tukkiminen, myös soille kasvaneiden vieraslajipuiden poistaminen. Kun puuston varjostava ja vettä sitova vaikutus häviää, vapautuu elintilaa alkuperäisille suobiotooppien lajeille. Poistettavan puuston määrä riippuu tavoitellusta lopputilasta sekä alueen alkuperäisestä suotyypistä.

"Olisi luontevaa suunnata hakkuita erityisesti soiden ennallistamisalueille, jolloin samaan aikaan saataisiin puuta, tuettaisiin suoluonnon ennallistamista ja säästettäisiin arvokkaampaa luontoa sekä koskemattomia luonnonmetsiä hakkuilta", sanoo Harjanne tiedotteessa.

title: Wikipedistiksi kurssin kautta?
content: Pitkän linjan wikipedistinä olen vuosien ajan yrittänyt houkutella tuttuja ja tuntemattomia Wikipedian muokkaajiksi, sillä Wikipediaa hienompaa yhteistyöprojektia on vaikea löytää. Usein olen kuitenkin saanut samansuuntaisia vastauksia. Yksi ei välttämättä tiedä, että kuka tahansa voi muokata. Toinen arvelee, ettei pysty tarjoamaan Wikipedialle mitään lisäarvoa. Kolmas on ehkä kiinnostunut, mutta ei tiedä mistä aloittaa. Vuosien varrella olen ollut monessa muokkaustapahtumassa opettamassa vasta-alkajille Wikipedian saloja. Jo päivän tai muutaman tunnin aikana on saatu ahaa-elämyksiä ja onnistumisen riemua, kun ensimmäinen ikioma Wikipedia-artikkeli on julkaistu kaikkien nähtäville. Silti itselleni on usein jäänyt tunne: voi kun olisi aikaa perehtyä muokkaamiseen tarkemminkin. Entä jos Wikipedian muokkaamisen voisi oppia kurssin kautta?

title: Wiki Loves Monuments: workshop & skrivstuga
content:
I september arrangerar vi den svenska grenen av Wiki Loves Monuments – en internationell fototävling där du bidrar till fri kunskap genom att fotografera det skyddade kulturarvet. Vi ordnar tävlingen i samarbete med Arbetslivsmuseernas samarbetsråd, vilket vi är väldigt glada över.

För att delta i tävlingen måste varje bild föreställa någon av Sveriges fornminnen, byggnadsminnen, K-märkta skepp/fritidsbåtar, kulturreservat eller arbetslivsmuseer. Bilderna släpps fria för hela världen att använda under Creative Commons-licens. Tack vare fokuset på just det skyddade kulturarvet byggs det upp en värdefull bildsamling som kan användas av exempelvis kulturarvsinstitutioner, journalister och forskare som vill synliggöra det skyddade kulturarvet.

Olidans kraftverk vid Göta älv i Trollhättan, Sverige Fotograf: Simiha, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

  • Leta fram ett foto du tagit på det skyddade kulturarvet – eller gå ut och ta nya bilder.
  • Skapa ett konto på Wikimedia Commons (tar cirka 30 sekunder), om du inte redan har ett.
  • Ladda upp bilden via kartan eller uppladdningsverktyget. Du kan ladda upp hur många bilder du vill till och med 30 september.

title: "Hope Is the Thing with Feathers": Rhiannon Giddens on New Album, AI, Ed Sheeran, Macklemore & Trump
content:
“If we don’t connect those dots between the struggles, we’re never going to get anywhere,” says Pulitzer Prize- and Grammy-winning multi-instrumentalist Rhiannon Giddens. “That’s what music is for. … We have to make music with people from different backgrounds, because then we have that conversation.”

Giddens has had a wide-spanning career, including her time with The Carolina Chocolate Drops, an old-time Black string band, and her work as a musical consultant on Ryan Coogler’s landmark film Sinners. She won a Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2023 for her opera Omar about Omar ibn Said, a Muslim scholar in Africa who was sold into slavery in the 1800s. Her new album, Hope Is the Thing with Feathers, comes out on Friday.

title: How to Limit What Apple’s New Siri AI Can Access in iOS 27
content:
Apple’s new operating system is here, and along with it comes a new version of Siri, dubbed with two very familiar letters: AI. As the name suggests, this Siri power-up resembles an AI chatbot more than the often derided voice assistant you might be used to. It has even evolved from a blob you invoke with a verbal command or a button press to a whole app. This update comes with a slew of privacy complications, but you can take some control over what this new Siri can access and use. 

There’s no denying that the new version of Siri is far more powerful than it used to be, and arguably more useful at surfacing details on your phone. But that comes at the cost of deeper access. Once enabled, Siri and Spotlight are combined, unifying the interface. Where you may have once just pulled down on the screen to search for an app or contact, you’re now also invoking Siri. 

Spotlight and Siri are now visually one and the same.

title: A State of the Union bereft of coherence and clarity
content:
The State of the Union is a very special exercise for the president of the European Commission. Its main purpose is to show that the Commission has a clear vision to tackle the numerous challenges and perils the Union is facing, and that, despite the complex environment, there is an experienced pilot at the helm. Indeed, this year’s statement takes place at an exceptionally difficult time, as President Ursula von der Leyen has said from the outset. Her description and diagnosis of the geopolitical and internal challenges and transformation are accurate enough. But what about her answers and political solutions?

Von der Leyen likes to use a certain degree of pathos to appeal to emotions. That is why she invites some special guests to materialise these emotions. One may doubt if pathos is the best way to respond to people’s fears and expectations and to gain trust.

title: Oversight Reports Echo HRW Findings on US Immigration Abuses
content:
On September 11, the US Department of Homeland Security’s Office of Inspector General published reports outlining findings from visits to Krome North Service Processing Center and the now-shuttered “Alligator Alcatraz,” immigration detention facilities in Florida. The oversight body found that the facilities failed to comply with DHS standards, including for medical care, environmental health and safety, and—in the case of Krome—use of force.

One of the most disturbing findings at Alligator Alcatraz was the use of “small metal enclosures”—essentially cages—to hold detainees for up to two hours, which the inspector general said “does not align with standards for humane treatment.” The report states that in at least one case, this may have been used as a “disciplinary tool.”

The inspector general said that confining people in cages “presents significant risks to detainee health and well-being.”

While Alligator Alcatraz officially closed on June 25, there are more than 200 active immigration detention facilities throughout the United States. Human Rights Watch has found cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatment at several of these facilities, including Krome.

title: 5 Henkilötietojen käsittelyperusteet
content:
Tietosuoja-asetuksen mukaan henkilötietoja saa käsitellä vain silloin, kun käsittelylle on laista löytyvä käsittelyperuste. Tämä käsittelyperuste on määritettävä ennen henkilötietojen käsittelyn aloittamista, ja sitä ei voi vaihtaa kesken käsittelyn. Käsittelyperuste kytkeytyy siihen, mihin tarkoitukseen tietoja käytetään. Tietosuoja-asetuksen 6 artikla määrittelee seuraavat käsittelyperusteet, joilla henkilötietojen käsittely on mahdollista:

  • rekisteröidyn suostumus
  • sopimus
  • rekisterinpitäjän lakisääteinen velvoite
  • elintärkeiden etujen suojaaminen
  • yleistä etua koskeva tehtävä tai julkinen valta
  • rekisterinpitäjän tai kolmannen osapuolen oikeutettu etu.

title: Iraq Sentences Former Electricity Director General to Seven Years for illicit enrichment
content:
An Iraqi anti-corruption court has sentenced the former director general of a state electricity distribution firm to seven years in prison for illicit enrichment, ordering him to forfeit nearly $20 million in restitution and fines as part of a sweeping crackdown on graft in the country’s power sector.

The official, Alaa Samir Rashid Shukr Al-Jubouri, who headed the state-owned General Company of Electricity Distribution (Middle Region), was convicted by Iraq’s Central Criminal Court for Combating Corruption. According to the country’s Integrity Commission, Rashid amassed unexplained wealth exceeding 5.5 billion Iraqi dinars (about $4.2 million) along with an additional $5.5 million in U.S. currency.

The court ordered Rashid to return the illicit gains and levied an equivalent fine, bringing his total financial liability to approximately $19.4 million. Judges also upheld a freeze on his movable and immovable assets, paving the way for seizure.

title: Tennessee Lawmakers Demand Answers on Safety in State Youth Prisons
content:
Four Democratic Tennessee state lawmakers sent a letter to the Department of Children’s Services demanding answers about safety and oversight in the state’s juvenile justice facilities.

The letter cites a recent WPLN and ProPublica investigation that found that juvenile justice facilities run by Tennessee businessman Jason Crews repeatedly failed to report abuse of children and other serious incidents to the state as required. The reporting involved interviews with dozens of former staff and youth, along with a review of emergency call logs, company records and state documents. Crews and his company Wayne Halfway House run all three of the state’s highest-security youth prisons. 

“The allegations that serious physical and sexual abuse, dangerous restraints, injuries, and other critical incidents have gone unreported by WHH demand an urgent, transparent, and independently verifiable response from the Department of Children’s Services,” lawmakers wrote.
